General:
	Elegance, grace, precision, and skill come together in one of the most popular events at the Olympic Winter Games. Here’s everything you need to know about figure skating at Milano Cortina 2026.

Competition events:
	Figure skating perfectly showcases the technical and physical abilities of its incredible performers. Whether solo or in pairs, figure skaters demonstrate balance and control on the ice, setting beautiful routines to music. It is a combination of athleticism and top-notch technical skill. The figure skating competitions at Milano Cortina 2026 will include five events. 

Olympic history:
	Figure skating is the oldest sport at the Olympic Winter Games, but made its Olympic debut at the summer edition of the Games at London 1908 and again in Antwerp in 1920. Since 1972, there have been events in men’s and women’s singles and a pairs competition. Ice dance was added in 1976. There have been events in men's singles, women’s singles, and pairs skating at every edition of the Olympic Winter Games. Ice dance was added in 1976, with a team competition introduced at Sochi 2014.

Rules:
	Figure skating includes five disciplines: men’s singles, women’s singles, pairs, ice dance, and the team competition. In the men’s, women’s, and pairs events, skaters perform two programs, a short program with required technical elements and a free program that also contains mandatory elements but allows more creative freedom, and both programs use music chosen by the athletes. Pairs must perform elements such as jumps and parallel spins together with strong synchronization, while ice dance differs by excluding jumps and overhead lifts and focusing instead on rhythm, precision, and choreography. Ice dance consists of a rhythm dance, with a music style selected each year by the International Skating Union, and a free dance that offers more artistic flexibility. Scoring is determined by a technical panel that identifies each element and its difficulty level, along with nine judges who evaluate execution quality and artistic components, and the combined scores from both programs determine the final results. The team competition has a qualifying phase and a final phase, both using the traditional short program and free skate, and during qualification each nation presents a male skater, female skater, pair, and ice dance team performing their short programs to earn points. This event takes place before the Opening Ceremony and is limited to the top ten countries in the seasonal world ranking.
